Set up analysis

Choose footage and sampling settings.

Use intervals of 250 ms or less. T numbers follow provisional paths; identities can swap during overlap. Dashed † centers are uncertain estimates. With the center rule below, recent paths can help separate an overlap for up to one second after a clear observation.

Optional: only discard candidates when the count exceeds the known fish count. Pink × marks show excluded candidates. A real fish at the edge can also be excluded; review the choices in Human analysis. Touching fish are checked before this rule chooses the nearest candidates. Splits can use two visible dark bodies or the preceding observed sample (up to 250 ms apart); † centers remain estimates. The center is the middle of the crop rectangle.

Works best with a fixed camera. Include the fish’s swimming area, then mask wall reflections. Fewer than five blobs may mean fish overlap; extra blobs may come from tank edges or reflections.

Model settings Roboflow InferenceJS

Using zebrafish_in_aquarium/9, a trained YOLOv8n model for zebrafish. Enter a Roboflow workspace publishable key, never a private API key.

Labeling uses your crop and frame interval. You can start without running detection.

Calibrate from a known length

Draw along a known distance in the preview, enter its length in inches, then use the scale.

Measure several grid squares near the swimming area for better accuracy. Perspective makes distances approximate. Clearing the line keeps the applied scale.

Include the space where fish swim, even above the floor. Choose “Mask reflection area” and drag over reflections to exclude them. Red masks apply to every frame and also exclude real fish that enter those areas. Changing a mask requires analyzing again.

How metrics work

Each detection center is a candidate fish position. Centers within the link distance form connected groups; a chain of links can join fish farther apart. Single fish are shown separately. The random comparison places the same number of points uniformly inside the selected tank crop, excluding reflection masks, 399 times and compares mean nearest-neighbor distance. A low percentile means tighter spacing than those random placements in that frame; adjacent video frames are not independent tests. Inch estimates use the paper-grid calibration and are approximate. When the detected count is low, the detector checks close to the crop edge, then may split a large joined region. These estimates are marked in the raw export. Reflections can create extras. Background tracking follows provisional paths across nearby frames; dashed † positions are uncertain and need review. Read the full method.

HUMAN ANALYSIS

Review sampled frames

Click the center of each visible fish in the usable area. Click one of your numbered marks to remove it. Review labels belong to each frame; they do not track individual fish across time.

← Back to analysis

Compare fish and reflections

Higher S usually means sharper edges. Scores are not probabilities or a 0–100 scale. Grid lines, contrast, noise, and motion can affect them. Compare candidates from the same recording.

# is a candidate ID within this frame; group numbers are separate. * means the scoring patch was clipped by the crop or a mask. “—” means too few pixels or no usable box. † marks an uncertain overlap estimate. T numbers identify provisional paths across frames, not verified fish identities; check estimates against neighboring frames.

Label candidates as fish or reflections to compare their scores across frames. Labels stay in this tab until results are cleared or the tab reloads; export them to keep them. Labels do not filter detections. Pink × marks and “No (outer)” identify candidates excluded by the optional center rule.

TRAINING DATA

Label fish in selected frames

Click to place one box per real fish. Adjust each box to enclose the whole fish, including overlapping fish separately. Leave reflections unlabeled. Reflection masks from analysis do not apply here.

← Back to analysis
—

Choose a fish button to select an overlapping box. In Move or resize mode, drag inside a box to move it or drag a corner to resize it. Width and height also adjust the selected box. Editing a labeled frame makes it a draft until you mark it labeled again.

Choose training frames

You can skip any frames. Only explicitly labeled frames enter the dataset. Label an empty frame only when it contains no real fish. Arrow keys navigate; L toggles labeled status when you are not typing in a control.

Dataset ZIP: clean cropped PNGs, YOLO boxes, and a JSON annotation manifest. Skipped and draft frames are excluded. Save progress JSON includes drafts and images for resuming with this video, crop, and interval; restoring it replaces this labeling project's current marks.
